specification.problem: Approximate e^{-iHt} on a small d-sparse Hermitian H (n-qubit system) with error eps, by an LCU of Szegedy/Berry-Childs quantum-walk powers weighted by Bessel functions J_m(tau), given black-box sparse-access oracles O_H (entries) and O_F (column indices).
specification.reconstruction_scope: One tiny instance: a single segment with tau=O(1) (e.g. n=1 or 2, d<=2), truncated at M chosen numerically, one LCU round plus optionally one round of oblivious amplitude amplification. Out of scope: the full multi-segment complexity analysis, the new lower bound proof, the exact oracle-level walk construction for general sparse H, and gate-count optimality.

symbols.meaning: d-sparse Hermitian Hamiltonian on n qubits
product of t, d, and H_max
quantum-walk unitary built from O_H and O_F
Bessel function of first kind, order m
truncation order of the Jacobi-Anger sum

symbols.domain: normalized vector on neighbor register plus sink

equations.label: Walk state
equations.description: States whose span is reflected about to define the walk; the amplitude sign/phase convention is an assumption (Hermitian entries may need phase handling).
equations.abstract_quote: Hamiltonian simulation via a quantum walk
equations.justification: Walk construction is named in the abstract; the explicit form is recalled from Berry-Childs, not stated in it.
assumptions: entries taken nonnegative or phases handled by O_H

equations.label: Walk eigenphases
equations.description: Walk eigenvalues on the invariant subspace tied to eigenvalue lambda of H.
equations.justification: Recalled Szegedy/Berry-Childs relation; the abstract does not state it.
assumptions: input embedded in the invariant subspace
the sign branch is fixed by the initial projection

equations.label: Jacobi-Anger
equations.justification: Standard identity; the abstract mentions only Bessel-function coefficients.

equations.label: Hamiltonian as walk-power sum
equations.description: Truncated LCU target; the restriction and sign handling are assumed. Negative m uses W^dagger.
equations.abstract_quote: By implementing a linear combination of quantum walk steps with coefficients given by Bessel functions
equations.justification: Combining eq_2 and eq_3 gives this relation; the abstract states the linear combination only in words.
assumptions: the odd/even branch signs for m<0 and the (±1)^m factor are handled by the initial projection or a Z-type correction

equations.label: LCU success amplitude
equations.description: Postselection amplitude on index register |0> after prepare, controlled-W^m, unprepare, with state prep amplitudes sqrt|J_m|/sqrt(sum|J_m|).
equations.justification: Standard LCU; the sketch says this is O(1) per segment with tau/r=O(1).
assumptions: one round of oblivious amplitude amplification then needs the LCU normalization to be near 2, which this sum does not give exactly; verify numerically

registers.name: idx
registers.role: LCU index register for m in [-M,M] (offset or sign-bit encoding)

specification.initial_state: |psi>_sys |0>_nbr |0>_idx |0>_flag, with the input embedded in the walk's invariant subspace

steps.description: Build W from O_H and O_F: prepare |psi_j>, reflect about their span, apply SWAP. One W costs O(1) oracle queries. Each placement of the placeholder counts as a query.
Classically compute J_m(tau) for |m|<=M, choosing M numerically so that the tail is below eps; set the LCU weights sqrt|J_m|.
Prepare the index register with standard rotation gates (not initialize), with sign bits phase-correcting negative Bessel values.
Apply controlled-W^m via a controlled-W ladder (W^dagger for m<0), then unprepare the index register.
Project/postselect idx=|0>, or apply one round of oblivious amplitude amplification per segment if tau/r=O(1); the output system state should approximate e^{-iHt}|psi>.

specification.measurement: If the runner reads the statevector, do not measure; compare the system state with idx and flag in |0>. If counts are required, measure only sys in the computational basis.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Compute fidelity against the classically computed expm(-iHt)|psi>; precompute J_m(tau) and choose M.
assumptions: Tiny instance chosen by us since no scope was given
H Hermitian with oracles as given, entries in the walk are real nonnegative or phases are handled
Coefficients are precomputed and loaded via rotation gates
Sign/branch ambiguity resolved by the initial projection
Segmentation and oblivious amplitude amplification are acceptable
